text.title: event-sourcing-basics Core Rules
text.summary: 12 testable rules grounding the event-sourcing-basics methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Once written, an event is never modified or deleted. Replays must produce identical state given the same event sequence.
rule.rationale: Mutable events destroy the audit trail and break replay determinism.

rule.statement: Events name what HAPPENED in past tense (OrderPlaced, PaymentCaptured). Never imperative (PlaceOrder is a command, not an event).
Apply via dispatch (_apply / handle_<EventClass>); never inline state mutation in command handlers.
rule.rationale: Inline mutation skips replay, breaks audit-trail equivalence.

rule.statement: Version increments by 1 per event applied. Concurrent appends use optimistic concurrency on expected_version.
rule.rationale: Optimistic concurrency is the only safe append model for an event-sourced stream.

rule.statement: Event schema evolution is planned upfront: additive fields with sensible defaults; new event versions get new class names (OrderPlacedV2).
rule.rationale: Replays cross historical schemas; ad-hoc evolution breaks them.

rule.statement: Events must be immutable (frozen=True). Once persisted, an event is never modified — it is the source of truth.
rule.rationale: Mutable events invalidate the audit log and break replay: if the stored event differs from what actually happened, replayed state diverges from original state.

rule.statement: Events are granular: one event per state change. Never use a catch-all UpdatedEvent with a full-state payload.
rule.rationale: Granular events make the intent explicit, allow targeted projections to subscribe only to relevant changes, and keep schema evolution manageable.

rule.statement: Name events in past tense describing what happened: OrderCreated, OrderItemAdded, OrderPlaced, OrderShipped, OrderCancelled.
rule.rationale: Past tense signals immutability and distinguishes events (facts) from commands (intentions).

rule.statement: State changes happen only through events. The aggregate applies events to itself via _apply(event); it never mutates fields directly in command methods.
rule.rationale: If command methods mutate state directly, replay from events produces different state than the live object, destroying the event-sourcing guarantee.

rule.statement: New events generated by command methods are added to _pending_events. They are not yet persisted. The repository drains pending events and appends them to the event store.
rule.rationale: Separating generation from persistence allows the repository to apply optimistic concurrency before appending, preventing lost-update bugs.

rule.statement: from_events(order_id, events) reconstructs the aggregate from stored history by replaying each event with is_new=False. is_new=False means the event is not added to _pending_events.
rule.rationale: Distinguishing new events from historical events prevents the repository from re-appending already-persisted events on the next save.

rule.statement: Skip when the input does not satisfy the Applies-If preconditions or another methodology owns this output shape.
rule.rationale: Prevents duplicate work and wrong-tool application.
